feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications/strategy and credible progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across skills sections, and could show sharper business impact through more quantified outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently position you as a digital strategy and communications leader.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions within one organization strongly support leadership growth and increasing scope.  
- Good specificity: tools, platforms, and responsibilities are concrete, especially around Drupal, analytics, multimedia, and governance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond scope metrics: include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, conversion improvements, cost savings, team size, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily; consolidating would improve structure and save space.  
- Tighten writing for consistency: use serial commas consistently (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; “organization-wide” and bullet punctuation/style should remain fully consistent throughout.

No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and anchoring it more clearly to senior leadership, public-sector/advocacy work, and digital transformation would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience in mission-driven and public-sector organizations.”
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper value statement focused on cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving cross-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and building scalable editorial and digital systems. Translates complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content that supports engagement and organizational goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- Avoid repeating channel lists here since Work Experience already provides that detail.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, senior-level phrasing: Digital Strategy & Transformation • Cross-Channel Communications Leadership • CMS & Web Platform Administration • Editorial Operations & Workflow Design • Analytics, Reporting & Optimization • Systems Architecture & Process Improvement • Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Coordination • Advocacy & Policy Communications • Multimedia & Live Event Production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-Channel Communications Leadership” for stronger grammar and scope.
- Change “Workflow & systems architecture” to “Systems Architecture & Process Improvement” to sound clearer and less technical-jargony.
- Consider replacing “Web & CMS administration” with “Web Platform Governance & CMS Administration” if you want to stress oversight, not just maintenance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header summary.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while Topline/Technical sections carry the specifics.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or adoption signals.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused statements, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and member-facing resource toolkits.”
- “Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”
- “Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.”
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the footer project summaries; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the examples.
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope-and-impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize biggest wins first: website migration, analytics infrastructure, video studio, then governance/operations.
- Tighten channel bullet and add outcomes if available: open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing, e.g., “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a higher strategic level here.
- Video expansion may partially duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as building enterprise studio capacity and in-house production infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms”
- Make the list more distinctive and concise, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Audience-centered content strategy and campaign planning

- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points like “10,000+ page migration” or “3.5M annual page views” into experience bullets rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets on editorial planning and coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations/automation, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- De-emphasize older or lower-signal items here; move WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and jQuery to “Technical + IT” only.
- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with impact-oriented language if space allows: “Enterprise web delivery” or “Platform modernization & integrations.”
- If you want one proof point, add a brief qualifier: “Drupal platform leadership for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating all three verbatim elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”

- “SEO and performance analysis” is close to “performance optimization”; choose one phrasing for consistency.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level and recency, e.g.: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize most relevant platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but Drupal should clearly lead given recent experience.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for concision.
- Best stronger version: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere; consider dropping it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, front-end troubleshooting, and CMS implementation support
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent work
- If space allows, add one proof point in a nearby project/role instead of here, e.g., “used to support Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and lightweight workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so don’t imply GitHub Actions duplicates that category unless you specify CI/CD or deployment support

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around automation/orchestration.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance/technical depth: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp”
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If you’ve built notable automations, consider replacing one lower-value collaboration tool with a qualifier: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate, Zapier…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; if space is tight, they’re weaker than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter and campaign automation
- Keep newest/most enterprise-relevant platform first; if Dynamics was the primary recent system, preserve that order.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign management” language here if those points are already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat automation terminology already listed under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you specify email-specific automation.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundation-building phase: team formation, early channel operations, and concrete production contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes where possible: website refresh support, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the closing clause to show light management: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital staff member.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles, helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs and helped expand digital storytelling efforts.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and stress ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer action, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid leaning too heavily on general digital content/video language already covered in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat “supporting organizational programs and policy work” if similar policy/advocacy support appears elsewhere; keep this entry focused on innovation projects + first podcast launch.
